record.paper_title: Open questions and perspectives for hadron electromagnetic form factors in space-like and time-like regions.
record.context_brief: Unified proton and neutron form-factor models across space-like and time-like regions
record.original_question: Can nucleon electromagnetic form factor models be constructed or identified that reproduce the full set of proton and neutron electric and magnetic form factors in both the space-like scattering region, where the virtual-photon momentum transfer satisfies t = -Q^2 < 0 and the form factors are real functions of Q^2, and the time-like annihilation region e+ + e- ↔ nucleon + antinucleon, where q^2 = -Q^2 > 0 and the form factors are complex?

evidence.quote: Elastic electron hadron scattering is considered the most direct way to access to FFs, which contain the information on the ground state of the hadron.
In this case, FFs are real functions of one variable, the four momentum squared of the virtual photon, t = −Q2 < 0.
Annihilation processes, as e+ + e− ↔ N + N¯, also give access to the nucleon FFs, but in another kinematical region, where FFs are complex functions of the momentum transfer squared, q2 = −Q2 > 0.
• are there models which can reproduce now all FFs for proton and neutron, in SL and TL regions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G_E^p(q^2), G_M^p(q^2), G_E^n(q^2), G_M^n(q^2)$ denote the Sachs electric and magnetic form factors of the proton and neutron, viewed as functions of the squared four-momentum transfer $q^2$ carried by a virtual photon coupling to the nucleon. In the space-like region $q^2 = -Q^2 < 0$, accessible through elastic electron–nucleon scattering, these form factors are real-valued functions of $Q^2$. In the time-like region $q^2 > 0$, accessible through annihilation processes such as $e^+ e^- \leftrightarrow N\bar{N}$ above threshold $q^2 \geq 4 M_N^2$, the form factors become complex-valued analytic functions, related to the space-like values by analytic continuation and constrained by causality, analyticity, and unitarity (with imaginary parts arising from on-shell intermediate hadronic states).

Construct, or determine whether there exists, a single theoretical model (parametrization) of the four nucleon Sachs form factors $G_{E,M}^{p,n}(q^2)$ that simultaneously reproduces, within experimental uncertainties, the full body of measured data in both the space-like region (proton and neutron, electric and magnetic) and the time-like region (modulus and, where available, phase or ratio $|G_E/G_M|$ of proton and neutron form factors), respecting the standard analyticity and asymptotic constraints (including perturbative QCD scaling at large $|q^2|$ and the correct normalizations $G_E^p(0)=1$, $G_M^p(0)=\mu_p$, $G_E^n(0)=0$, $G_M^n(0)=\mu_n$).
artifact.status_search_result: Several models (extended Lomon–Gari–Krümpelmann vector-meson-dominance fits, two-component quark-core plus meson-cloud parametrizations, and extended VMD models with analyticity/unitarity constraints) have been proposed and provide unified fits of proton and neutron electromagnetic form factors in both space-like and time-like regions with reasonable success. However, tensions remain (e.g., oscillatory features in the time-like region, neutron time-like data, and the proton $|G_E/G_M|$ ratio), so the question is partially solved rather than fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Timelike and spacelike electromagnetic form factors of nucleons, a unified description
status_evidence.snippet: Extended Lomon-Gari-Krümpelmann model performs a unified fit to all nucleon electromagnetic form factor data in spacelike and timelike regions.
status_evidence.claim: A unified VMD-based model fits proton and neutron form factors in both regions.

status_evidence.title: A model for space and time-like proton (neutron) form factors
status_evidence.snippet: Two-component model with intrinsic quark structure and meson cloud analyzing space- and time-like nucleon form factors.
status_evidence.claim: Two-component models partially achieve unified description.

status_evidence.title: Extended vector meson dominance model for nucleon EM form factors
status_evidence.snippet: Updated eVMD model with predictions for electromagnetic nucleon radii and couplings respecting analyticity.
status_evidence.claim: Recent eVMD parametrizations continue to refine unified descriptions.

status_evidence.title: Understanding oscillating features of time-like nucleon EM form factors
status_evidence.snippet: Oscillating features of time-like nucleon form factors studied within extended VMD; remaining structures not fully explained.
status_evidence.claim: Open issues remain in the time-like region, indicating only partial resolution.
